You are an autonomous simulation agent with access to a Linux shell, a writable working directory, and CalculiX CrunchiX (`ccx`). Your job is to run the CalculiX analysis defined by the input deck provided below, without changing the physics.

    Job name: `case_102` (the input file must be named `case_102.inp`).

    What to do
    1) Create the file `case_102.inp` in the working directory with the exact contents given in the `Input deck` section below.
2) Run CalculiX using either `ccx -i case_102` or `ccx case_102` (use whichever works on your system).
3) Determine whether the run succeeded by checking `case_102.sta` (look for a successful termination such as 'JOB COMPLETED').
4) Write a `results.json` file (in the working directory) with the schema:
{
  "solver": "calculix",
  "case_id": "case_102",
  "status": "success" | "error",
  "ccx_version": "...",
  "artifacts": [],
  "notes": "..."
}
In `ccx_version`, record the version string from `ccx -v` (or the closest equivalent). In `notes`, record the exact ccx command you used, and if the run failed, include the error message and what file indicated the failure.

    Case description (for context; the authoritative definition is the input deck)
    This code defines a finite element model of a cantilever beam using CalculiX, a software for structural analysis. The model starts with a heading that includes the model name and date. It specifies the coordinates of nodes in a 3D space, followed by the definition of 20-node brick elements (C3D20R) that make up the beam. The elements are grouped into a set named "B1". A node set "CN7" is defined, which includes specific nodes, and boundary conditions are applied to restrict movement in certain directions. The material properties are defined under the name "HY" with an elastic modulus of 210,000 and a Poisson's ratio of 0.3. The solid section of the beam is assigned this material. Additional node sets "LAST" and "GIBO" are defined, with "GIBO" having a specific boundary condition applied to it. The analysis step is set to perform a nonlinear geometric calculation with 50 increments, using a static analysis procedure. The boundary condition for the "GIBO" node set specifies a small displacement in the third direction. Finally, the code instructs the program to print the displacements of all nodes and the stress results for all elements.
